title: Clicking a label does not focus its input
summary: The labels are not tied to their inputs, so a click does not focus them and a screen reader has no name to read. Connect them with for and id, and give the buttons a type.

files.content: I agree to the terms

turns.user: signup form, clicking the Email text doesnt put the cursor in the box. also someone said VoiceOver just reads "edit text"

assistant.body: Great catch. Both come from the same place: the browser does not know which label belongs to which input. Put the input's id in the label's for attribute and the two are linked. A click on the label then focuses the input, and a screen reader reads the label as its name. Note: name is what gets submitted, and it plays no part in this link. For a checkbox sitting next to its text, wrapping both in a label is enough.

turns.user: works. also just noticed Show submits the form?? why

assistant.body: A button inside a form is a submit button unless it says otherwise, so every click on Show sent the form. A button that only toggles something gets type="button". The real submit button gets type="submit" too, so the intent is written down. In short, give every button in a form a type.

<button type="button" onclick="togglePassword()">Show</button>
<button type="submit" class="bg-blue-600 text-white">Sign up</button>
